_: PRE-REGISTERED seat-decomposition experiment (Matt, 2026-08-19): can cheap seats reach the governs-aspect floor when the 8-way choice is decomposed into INDEPENDENT per-aspect binaries? Written BEFORE any experimental call. Pure seat R&D: the certified frontier layer (assert_signature.json) is the ground truth and is NOT modified.
sample: seed 20260821, 100 asserts drawn from all 985 keys (sorted order)

protocol.deepseek: 8 independent one-shot API calls per assert; byte-identical shared prefix (span+norm) with the per-aspect question appended (aspect-inner loop for prompt-cache hits); strict question: 'is <aspect> a PRIMARY constraint of this norm - what the norm is about, not an incidental benefit?' yes/no.
protocol.haiku: 8 ASPECT-SPECIALIST agents, each answering one aspect's binary for all 100 items - cross-aspect independence is structural (different agents), which a per-item transcript would compromise (anchoring; pre-registered rationale in transcript 2026-08-19).
protocol.assembly: MECHANICAL, fixed here: label = set of yes-aspects; cardinality 1-2 = label stands; 0 or >=3 = anomaly (would escalate to frontier in production; scored here as automatic non-match unless the frontier label happens to equal the set).

metrics: exact-set agreement vs assert_signature.json governs (authority_plumbing NOT tested - already passes cheap at 0.97); over-listing rate (extra aspects) and under-listing rate (missing aspects) reported separately; anomaly rate reported.
floor: 0.85 exact-set for a seat to qualify for next-document aspect annotation; below floor, frontier default stands with this alternative rejected by measurement.
prediction: decomposition fixes the label-competition misses (authority-flag precedent: binary+crisp passed 0.97 where multiway failed); the open risk is yes-bias over-listing (v3 protects precedent). No directional prediction registered beyond: anomaly rate under 15% or the protocol is impractical regardless of accuracy.
